column3: Close to the Hebrew; The wish idiom “who will give you” is rendered “Oh that you were,” and “the suckling of my mother’s breasts” as “Who nursed at my mother’s breasts.”
“She taught me” (or “you will teach me”) is rendered “who used to instruct me,” and NASB joins the wine and juice (“spiced wine … from the juice”).
The Hebrew is a statement (“his left hand [is] under my head”); NASB renders it as a wish, “Let his left hand be.”
“Why will you awaken … arouse” is rendered “Do not arouse or awaken,” and “the love … until it pleases” as “my love, Until she pleases.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB divides the verse between speakers, and “aroused” is rendered “awakened.”
“A flame of Yah” is rendered “The very flame of the LORD,” taking the ending as the divine name.
Close to the Hebrew; “Certainly people will despise it” is rendered “It would be utterly despised.”
Close to the Hebrew; “We will shut up over her a board” is rendered “We shall barricade her with planks.”
Close to the Hebrew; The present “my breasts [are]” is rendered “were,” and “I was” as “I became.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Those who keep” is rendered “caretakers,” and NASB adds “shekels.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Before me” is rendered “at my disposal.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Dwells” is rendered “sit.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Hasten” is rendered “Hurry,” and “the fawn of the deer” as “a young stag.”
